text:
talia: hey all, onboarding day 2. running `make dev` (docker compose) but my Go server on the host can't reach Postgres. error: `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5432: connect: connection refused` even though `docker ps` shows the postgres container up.

ben: welcome! quick check: are you running your app on the host or in a container? Service names (like `db`) only resolve between containers.

talia: app is on the host to get fast file reloads. compose file had `ports:
  - "5432"` which I thought exposed it.

devex: small but annoying detail: `ports: - "5432"` publishes the container port but doesn't bind it to the host interface the way `"5432:5432"` does. Try mapping host->container explicitly.

talia: changed to `"5432:5432"` and recreated containers. `docker ps` now shows `0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp` but `psql -h localhost -p 5432` still refuses.

ben: run `lsof -i:5432` or `ss -ltnp | grep 5432` — could be a local Postgres already bound to that port on your machine.

talia: good call — `lsof` shows `postgres` running on host PID 2345. stopped the system Postgres and now host psql connects to the container. thank you.

devex: other options if you can’t stop local PG: map to a different host port like `"5433:5432"` and set your DB URL to `localhost:5433`. Or run your app inside a dev container so it can use `db:5432` directly (recommended for consistent env).

talia: noted. also saw permission errors earlier (`postmaster.pid permission denied`) because the repo used a host bind for data. switched to a named volume `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and that fixed it.

ben: yea named volumes avoid weird UID/GID issues across mac/linux/WSL.

devex: TL;DR for new-hires: 1) service names resolve only between containers; 2) use `"5432:5432"` to expose to host or a different host port to avoid collisions; 3) prefer named volumes for Postgres; 4) run app in a dev container for DNS + consistency. We have a `dev` compose profile that does this — `docker compose --profile dev up`. Ping @devex if you want the profile in your dotfiles.

talia: thanks everyone — stopping local PG fixed it. I'll add a short note to the README about port collisions and named volumes. :tada:

bot-deploy: (bot) postgres:14 started :white_check_mark:"
